title: A childhood tumor. Three spinal surgeries. Paralyzed at 29. She became India's first woman Paralympic medalist. October 5, 2026.
excerpt: From an 1864 cyclone that accidentally built India's weather service, to a Paralympic medalist who started training at 30 after paralysis, October 5's five stories are about systems and people that got stronger because something broke first.
bodyHtml:
Every story today starts with something failing - a city with no warning system, a company that got sold, an old diesel engine, a body paralyzed by surgery - and ends with something built stronger in its place: a national weather service, a foundation, a cleaner engine, a medal nobody expected.

October 5, 1864: a cyclone killed 60,000 people in Calcutta - and accidentally built India's weather-warning system

The Great Calcutta Cyclone sent a storm surge roughly 40 feet high up the Hooghly River, killing an estimated 60,000 people with no warning system in place. The disaster became one of the direct pressures that led to the founding of the India Meteorological Department on January 15, 1875.

She leads a global fight against violence toward women. In 2026, she became only the second South Asian in the National Women's Hall of Fame

Mona Sinha, CEO of Equality Now, was inducted into the National Women's Hall of Fame on September 24, 2026 - only the second South Asian ever, after Indra Nooyi. Her work secured 17 legal changes across nine countries in 2025 alone, benefiting an estimated 69 million women and girls.

She sold her tech company to a Fortune 200 firm. Then she built a foundation named after her mother

Rashi Mehta co-founded Rahi Systems in her Fremont garage in 2013; it grew to 25+ countries before Wesco acquired it. In 2024 she founded the Iron Lady Foundation, named for her mother Dr. Leela Mehta, one of Rajasthan's first gynecologists - now funding water systems, science labs and girls' education across rural Rajasthan.

India just ran its first train that burns less diesel by mixing in natural gas

India's first diesel-LNG dual-fuel train was flagged off September 27, 2026, between Sabarmati and Mahesana Junction, Gujarat - existing power cars retrofitted rather than replaced, cutting diesel use by roughly 40% on routes that aren't electrified yet.

A childhood tumor. Three spinal surgeries at 29. Paralyzed from the waist down. She took up competitive sport at 30 anyway

Deepa Malik was paralyzed from the waist down after a tumor recurrence and three spinal surgeries at 29. At the 2016 Rio Paralympics, at age 45, she won silver in shot put - becoming the first Indian woman to win a Paralympic medal, on top of 23 international and 58 national medals over her career.

Five stories, one thread: a tragedy that built an institution, a leader whose advocacy became law, a businesswoman who turned a sale into a mission, an old engine rebuilt to pollute less, and a body rebuilt into a medal-winning career. Nothing here stayed broken.
